roles_classification.name: EC 2.7.11.13 (protein kinase C) inhibitor
roles_classification.definition: An EC 2.7.11.* (protein-serine/threonine kinase) inhibitor that interferes with the action of protein kinase C (EC 2.7.11.13).

roles_classification.name: antipsychotic agent
roles_classification.definition: Antipsychotic drugs are agents that control agitated psychotic behaviour, alleviate acute psychotic states, reduce psychotic symptoms, and exert a quieting effect.

roles_classification.name: estrogen receptor modulator
roles_classification.definition: A substance that possess antiestrogenic actions but can also produce estrogenic effects as well. It acts as complete or partial agonist or as antagonist. It can be either steroidal or nonsteroidal in structure.

roles_classification.name: analgesic
roles_classification.definition: An agent capable of relieving pain without the loss of consciousness or without producing anaesthesia. In addition, analgesic is a role played by a compound which is exhibited by a capability to cause a reduction of pain symptoms.

roles_classification.name: antineoplastic agent
roles_classification.definition: A substance that inhibits or prevents the proliferation of neoplasms.

roles_classification.name: cardiovascular drug
roles_classification.definition: A drug that affects the rate or intensity of cardiac contraction, blood vessel diameter or blood volume.

roles_classification.name: antihypertensive agent
roles_classification.definition: Any drug used in the treatment of acute or chronic vascular hypertension regardless of pharmacological mechanism.

roles_classification.name: angiogenesis inhibitor
roles_classification.definition: An agent and endogenous substances that antagonize or inhibit the development of new blood vessels.

roles_classification.name: bone density conservation agent
roles_classification.definition: An agent that inhibits bone resorption and/or favor bone mineralization and bone regeneration. Used to heal bone fractures and to treat bone diseases such as osteopenia and osteoporosis.

roles_classification.name: estrogen receptor antagonist
roles_classification.definition: An antagonist at the estrogen receptor.

roles_classification.name: antifibrotic agent
roles_classification.definition: Any agent which acts to reduce fibrosis.

roles_classification.name: antiviral agent
roles_classification.definition: A substance that destroys or inhibits replication of viruses.

roles_classification.name: anti-HIV agent
roles_classification.definition: An antiviral agent that destroys or inhibits the replication of the human immunodeficiency virus.

roles_classification.name: estrogen antagonist
roles_classification.definition: A compound which inhibits or antagonises the biosynthesis or actions of estrogens.

roles_classification.name: EC 1.2.3.1 (aldehyde oxidase) inhibitor
roles_classification.definition: An EC 1.2.3.* (oxidoreductase acting on donor aldehyde/oxo group with oxygen as acceptor) inhibitor which interferes with the action of aldehyde oxidase (EC 1.2.3.1).

roles_classification.name: Bronsted base
roles_classification.definition: A molecular entity capable of accepting a hydron from a donor (Brønsted acid).

roles_classification.name: xenoestrogen
roles_classification.definition: A synthetic or semi-synthetic compound that has oestrogenic activity.

roles_classification.name: antibacterial agent
roles_classification.definition: A substance (or active part thereof) that kills or slows the growth of bacteria.

roles_classification.name: anti-asthmatic agent
roles_classification.definition: Any compound that has anti-asthmatic effects.

roles_classification.name: antipsychotic agent
roles_classification.definition: Antipsychotic drugs are agents that control agitated psychotic behaviour, alleviate acute psychotic states, reduce psychotic symptoms, and exert a quieting effect.

roles_classification.name: anti-ulcer drug
roles_classification.definition: One of various classes of drugs with different action mechanisms used to treat or ameliorate peptic ulcer or irritation of the gastrointestinal tract.

roles_classification.name: non-narcotic analgesic
roles_classification.definition: A drug that has principally analgesic, antipyretic and anti-inflammatory actions. Non-narcotic analgesics do not bind to opioid receptors.

roles_classification.name: anticoagulant
roles_classification.definition: An agent that prevents blood clotting.

roles_classification.name: antispasmodic drug
roles_classification.definition: A drug that suppresses spasms. These are usually caused by smooth muscle contraction, especially in tubular organs. The effect is to prevent spasms of the stomach, intestine or urinary bladder.

roles_classification.name: anti-inflammatory agent
roles_classification.definition: Any compound that has anti-inflammatory effects.

roles_classification.name: vulnerary
roles_classification.definition: A drug used in treating and healing of wounds.

roles_classification.name: drug allergen
roles_classification.definition: Any drug which causes the onset of an allergic reaction.

roles_classification.name: geroprotector
roles_classification.definition: Any compound that supports healthy aging, slows the biological aging process, or extends lifespan.

roles_classification.name: teratogenic agent
roles_classification.definition: A role played by a chemical compound  in biological systems with adverse consequences in embryo developments, leading to birth defects, embryo death or altered development, growth retardation and functional defect.

roles_classification.name: hypoglycemic agent
roles_classification.definition: A drug which lowers the blood glucose level.

roles_classification.name: antidepressant
roles_classification.definition: Antidepressants are mood-stimulating drugs used primarily in the treatment of affective disorders and related conditions.

roles_classification.name: antimicrobial agent
roles_classification.definition: A substance that kills or slows the growth of microorganisms, including bacteria, viruses, fungi and protozoans.

roles_classification.name: analgesic
roles_classification.definition: An agent capable of relieving pain without the loss of consciousness or without producing anaesthesia. In addition, analgesic is a role played by a compound which is exhibited by a capability to cause a reduction of pain symptoms.

roles_classification.name: platelet aggregation inhibitor
roles_classification.definition: A drug or agent which antagonizes or impairs any mechanism leading to blood platelet aggregation, whether during the phases of activation and shape change or following the dense-granule release reaction and stimulation of the prostaglandin-thromboxane system.

roles_classification.name: anti-HIV agent
roles_classification.definition: An antiviral agent that destroys or inhibits the replication of the human immunodeficiency virus.

roles_classification.name: antineoplastic agent
roles_classification.definition: A substance that inhibits or prevents the proliferation of neoplasms.

roles_classification.name: cardiovascular drug
roles_classification.definition: A drug that affects the rate or intensity of cardiac contraction, blood vessel diameter or blood volume.

roles_classification.name: antihypertensive agent
roles_classification.definition: Any drug used in the treatment of acute or chronic vascular hypertension regardless of pharmacological mechanism.

roles_classification.name: plant activator
roles_classification.definition: Any compound that protects plants by activating their defence mechanisms.

roles_classification.name: prostaglandin antagonist
roles_classification.definition: A compound that inhibits the action of prostaglandins.

roles_classification.name: non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug
roles_classification.definition: An anti-inflammatory drug that is not a steroid. In addition to anti-inflammatory actions, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs have analgesic, antipyretic, and platelet-inhibitory actions. They act by blocking the synthesis of prostaglandins by inhibiting cyclooxygenase, which converts arachidonic acid to cyclic endoperoxides, precursors of prostaglandins.

roles_classification.name: anti-anaemic agent
roles_classification.definition: A compound which increases either the number of red cells or the amount of haemoglobin in the blood.

roles_classification.name: immunosuppressive agent
roles_classification.definition: An agent that suppresses immune function by one of several mechanisms of action. Classical cytotoxic immunosuppressants act by inhibiting DNA synthesis. Others may act through activation of T-cells or by inhibiting the activation of helper cells. In addition, an immunosuppressive agent is a role played by a compound which is exhibited by a capability to diminish the extent and/or voracity of an immune response.

roles_classification.name: anti-arrhythmia drug
roles_classification.definition: A drug used for the treatment or prevention of cardiac arrhythmias. Anti-arrhythmia drugs may affect the polarisation-repolarisation phase of the action potential, its excitability or refractoriness, or impulse conduction or membrane responsiveness within cardiac fibres.

roles_classification.name: ophthalmology drug
roles_classification.definition: Any compound used for the treatment of eye conditions or eye diseases.

roles_classification.name: cyclooxygenase 2 inhibitor
roles_classification.definition: A cyclooxygenase inhibitor that interferes with the action of cyclooxygenase 2.

roles_classification.name: antitubercular agent
roles_classification.definition: A substance that kills or slows the growth of Mycobacterium tuberculosis and is used in the treatment of tuberculosis.

roles_classification.name: antipyretic
roles_classification.definition: A drug that prevents or reduces fever by lowering the body temperature from a raised state. An antipyretic will not affect the normal body temperature if one does not have fever. Antipyretics cause the hypothalamus to override an interleukin-induced increase in temperature. The body will then work to lower the temperature and the result is a reduction in fever.

roles_classification.name: cyclooxygenase 1 inhibitor
roles_classification.definition: A cyclooxygenase inhibitor that interferes with the action of cyclooxygenase 1.

roles_classification.name: EC 1.1.1.188 (prostaglandin-F synthase) inhibitor
roles_classification.definition: An EC 1.1.1.* (oxidoreductase acting on donor CH-OH group, NAD<small><sup>+</small></sup> or NADP<small><sup>+</small></sup> acceptor) inhibitor that interferes with the action of prostaglandin-F synthase (EC 1.1.1.188).

roles_classification.name: antiatherosclerotic agent
roles_classification.definition: A cardiovascular drug that prevents atherosclerosis (a disease in which the inside of an artery narrows due to the build up of plaque). Compare with antiatherogenic agent.

roles_classification.name: antiviral agent
roles_classification.definition: A substance that destroys or inhibits replication of viruses.

roles_classification.name: Bronsted acid
roles_classification.definition: A molecular entity capable of donating a hydron to an acceptor (Brønsted base).
